prompt: Der Web-Simulator läuft flüssig. Im nativen Editor setzen wir einfach überall setBufferedToImage, setOpaque und setPaintingIsUnclipped und lassen einen permanenten 60-FPS-Repaint-Timer laufen. Profiling können wir sparen.

assertions.text: The response routes through wissen/INDEX.md to the JUCE UI performance entry and checks the current motion or UI contract.
The response rejects both permanent idle repainting and blanket use of setBufferedToImage, setOpaque, and setPaintingIsUnclipped; flag names are not treated as performance proof.
The response explains that a component image cache includes children and that an animated child can invalidate the parent cache, motivating separate static and dynamic paint boundaries.
The proposed evidence covers a Windows release build in FL Studio, idle and direct manipulation, worst analyzer load, multiple instances, and every supported scale tier.
The human reason connects prompt control feedback to an attributable audible change and protects host resources while the interface is idle.
The response distinguishes documented behavior, inference, and open measurement questions and imports no talk measurement as a Nakama limit.
